items.t: Adults and children: acute bacterial sinusitis, acute streptococcal tonsillitis/pharyngitis, acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis/COPD, community-acquired pneumonia, acute otitis media, acute cystitis, acute pyelonephritis, asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy, typhoid/paratyphoid fever, dental abscess with spreading cellulitis, prosthetic joint infections, H. pylori eradication, Lyme disease.

src.q: Amoxicillin is indicated for the treatment of the following infections in adults and children

Acute bacterial sinusitis Acute streptococcal tonsillitis and pharyngitis Acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis (AECB)/acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) Community acquired pneumonia Acute otitis media Acute cystitis Acute pyelonephritis
Asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy Typhoid and paratyphoid fevers Dental abscess with spreading cellulitis Prosthetic joint infections Helicobacter pylori eradication Lyme disease

items.t: Prophylaxis of endocarditis.

src.q: Amoxicillin is also indicated for the prophylaxis of endocarditis.

restrictions.note: No specialist-only, shared-care or brand-specific prescribing restriction found in the amoxicillin SmPCs accessed. SmPCs advise considering official guidance on appropriate antibacterial use.

items.t: Acute bacterial sinusitis, asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy, acute pyelonephritis, dental abscess with spreading cellulitis, acute cystitis: 250 mg to 500 mg every 8 hours, or 750 mg to 1 g every 12 hours; severe infections 750 mg to 1 g every 8 hours. Acute cystitis may be treated with 3 g twice daily for one day.

src.q: 250 mg to 500 mg every 8 hours or 750 mg to 1 g every 12 hours For severe infections 750 mg to 1 g every 8 hours Acute cystitis may be treated with 3g twice daily for one day
Asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy Acute pyelonephritis Dental abscess with spreading cellulitis Acute cystitis

items.t: Acute otitis media, acute streptococcal tonsillitis/pharyngitis, acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis: 500 mg every 8 hours or 750 mg to 1 g every 12 hours; severe infections 750 mg to 1 g every 8 hours for 10 days.

src.q: Acute otitis media 500 mg every 8 hours, 750 mg to 1 g every 12 hours Acute streptococcal tonsillitis and pharyngitis Acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis For severe infections 750 mg to 1 g every 8 hours for 10 days

items.t: Community-acquired pneumonia: 500 mg to 1 g every 8 hours.

src.q: Community acquired pneumonia 500 mg to 1 g every 8 hours

items.t: Typhoid and paratyphoid fever: 500 mg to 2 g every 8 hours.

src.q: Typhoid and paratyphoid fever 500 mg to 2 g every 8 hours

items.t: Prosthetic joint infections: 500 mg to 1 g every 8 hours.

src.q: Prosthetic joint infections 500 mg to 1 g every 8 hours

items.t: Prophylaxis of endocarditis: 2 g orally as a single dose 30 to 60 minutes before the procedure.

src.q: Prophylaxis of endocarditis 2 g orally, single dose 30 to 60 minutes before procedure

items.t: H. pylori eradication: 750 mg to 1 g twice daily with a proton pump inhibitor and another antibiotic (e.g. clarithromycin or metronidazole) for 7 days.

src.q: 750 mg to 1 g twice daily in combination with a proton pump inhibitor (e.g. omeprazole, lansoprazole) and another antibiotic (e.g. clarithromycin, metronidazole) for 7 days

items.t: Lyme disease, early stage: 500 mg to 1 g every 8 hours (maximum 4 g/day in divided doses) for 14 days (10 to 21 days).

src.q: Early stage: 500 mg to 1 g every 8 hours up to a maximum of 4 g/day in divided doses for 14 days (10 to 21 days)

items.t: Lyme disease, late stage (systemic involvement): 500 mg to 2 g every 8 hours (maximum 6 g/day in divided doses) for 10 to 30 days.

src.q: Late stage (systemic involvement): 500 mg to 2 g every 8 hours up to a maximum of 6 g/day in divided doses for 10 to 30 days

items.t: Elderly: no dose adjustment considered necessary. Duration should generally be as short as possible and set by infection type and response.

src.q: Elderly No dose adjustment is considered necessary.
should generally be as short as possible

items.t: Children < 40 kg, acute bacterial sinusitis, acute otitis media, community-acquired pneumonia, acute cystitis, acute pyelonephritis, dental abscess: 20 to 90 mg/kg/day in divided doses.

src.q: Acute bacterial sinusitis 20 to 90 mg/kg/day in divided doses* Acute otitis media Community acquired pneumonia Acute cystitis Acute pyelonephritis Dental abscess with spreading cellulitis

items.t: Children < 40 kg, acute streptococcal tonsillitis and pharyngitis: 40 to 90 mg/kg/day in divided doses. Twice-daily regimens only when the dose is in the upper range.

src.q: Acute streptococcal tonsillitis and pharyngitis 40 to 90 mg/kg/day in divided doses*
Twice daily dosing regimens should only be considered when the dose is in the upper range.

items.t: Children < 40 kg, typhoid and paratyphoid fever: 100 mg/kg/day in three divided doses.

src.q: paratyphoid fever 100 mg/kg/day in three divided doses

items.t: Children < 40 kg, prophylaxis of endocarditis: 50 mg/kg orally as a single dose 30 to 60 minutes before the procedure.

src.q: Prophylaxis of endocarditis 50 mg/kg orally, single dose 30 to 60 minutes before procedure

items.t: Children < 40 kg, Lyme disease: early stage 25 to 50 mg/kg/day in three divided doses for 10 to 21 days; late stage (systemic involvement) 100 mg/kg/day in three divided doses for 10 to 30 days.

src.q: Early stage: 25 to 50 mg/kg/day in three divided doses for 10 to 21 days
Late stage (systemic involvement): 100 mg/kg/day in three divided doses for 10 to 30 days

items.t: Children weighing 40 kg or more take the adult dose.

src.q: Children weighing 40 kg or more should be prescribed the adult dosage.

items.t: Paediatric suspension is recommended for children under six months of age.

src.q: Amoxicillin Paediatric Suspension is recommended for children under six months of age.

items.t: Very young children (including preterm newborns) in the first week of life: dosing interval should not be more frequent than twice daily (immature renal elimination).

src.q: For very young children (including preterm newborns) in the first week of life the interval of administration should not exceed twice daily administration

items.t: Hypersensitivity to amoxicillin, to any penicillin or to any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance, to any of the penicillins or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: History of a severe immediate hypersensitivity reaction (e.g. anaphylaxis) to another beta-lactam (e.g. a cephalosporin, carbapenem or monobactam).

src.q: History of a severe immediate hypersensitivity reaction (e.g. anaphylaxis) to another beta-lactam agent (e.g. a cephalosporin, carbapenem or monobactam).

items.t: Acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP) on amoxicillin requires stopping it and contraindicates any later use.

src.q: This reaction requires amoxicillin discontinuation and contra-indicates any subsequent administration.

items.t: Ask carefully about previous hypersensitivity reactions to penicillins, cephalosporins or other beta-lactams before starting. Serious, occasionally fatal reactions are more likely with a history of penicillin hypersensitivity and in atopic people. Stop if an allergic reaction occurs.

src.q: careful enquiry should be made concerning previous hypersensitivity reactions to penicillins, cephalosporins or other beta-lactam agents
These reactions are more likely to occur in individuals with a history of penicillin hypersensitivity and in atopic individuals.
If an allergic reaction occurs, amoxicillin therapy must be discontinued and appropriate alternative therapy instituted.

items.t: Avoid if infectious mononucleosis (glandular fever) is suspected: morbilliform rash.

src.q: Amoxicillin should be avoided if infectious mononucleosis is suspected since the occurrence of a morbilliform rash has been associated with this condition following the use of amoxicillin.

items.t: Convulsions may occur with impaired renal function, high doses or predisposing factors (history of seizures, treated epilepsy, meningeal disorders).

src.q: Convulsions may occur in patients with impaired renal function or in those receiving high doses or in patients with predisposing factors (e.g. history of seizures, treated epilepsy or meningeal disorders

items.t: Drug-induced enterocolitis syndrome (DIES), mainly in children: protracted vomiting 1-4 hours after a dose without skin or respiratory allergy signs; severe cases can progress to shock.

src.q: Drug-induced enterocolitis syndrome (DIES) has been reported mainly in children receiving amoxicillin
There have been severe cases including progression to shock.

items.t: Hypersensitivity can progress to Kounis syndrome (allergic reaction that can cause myocardial infarction); chest pain with an allergic reaction may be a presenting symptom.

src.q: Hypersensitivity reactions can also progress to Kounis syndrome, a serious allergic reaction that can result in myocardial infarction

items.t: Consider antibiotic-associated colitis in anyone with diarrhoea during or after treatment; if it occurs stop amoxicillin. Anti-peristaltic medicines are contraindicated in this situation.

src.q: Should antibiotic-associated colitis occur, amoxicillin should immediately be discontinued, a physician consulted and an appropriate therapy initiated.
Anti-peristaltic medicinal products are contra-indicated in this situation.

items.t: Renal impairment: adjust dose to degree of impairment (see Renal).

src.q: In patients with renal impairment, the dose should be adjusted according to the degree of impairment

items.t: High doses: keep adequate fluid intake and urine output to reduce the risk of crystalluria; check patency of bladder catheters.

src.q: During the administration of high doses of amoxicillin, it is advisable to maintain adequate fluid intake and urinary output in order to reduce the possibility of amoxicillin crystalluria.

items.t: Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction can follow treatment of Lyme disease; it is common and usually self-limiting.

src.q: Patients should be reassured that this is a common and usually self-limiting consequence of antibiotic treatment of Lyme disease.

items.t: Not suitable for some infections unless the pathogen is known or very likely to be susceptible, particularly UTIs and severe ear, nose and throat infections.

src.q: This particularly applies when considering the treatment of patients with urinary tract infections and severe infections of the ear, nose and throat.

items.t: Urine glucose: use enzymatic glucose oxidase methods (false positives with chemical methods). May distort oestriol assays in pregnancy.

src.q: It is recommended that when testing for the presence of glucose in urine during amoxicillin treatment, enzymatic glucose oxidase methods should be used.
The presence of amoxicillin may distort assay results for oestriol in pregnant women.

items.t: Suspension contains sorbitol: patients with rare hereditary fructose intolerance should not take it. Contains sodium benzoate, which may increase the risk of jaundice in newborn babies.

src.q: This medicinal product contains sorbitol. Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance should not take this medicine.
May increase the risk of jaundice in newborn babies.

items.t: Warfarin / acenocoumarol (oral anticoagulants): raised INR reported. If used together, carefully monitor prothrombin time/INR when amoxicillin is added or stopped; anticoagulant dose may need adjusting.

src.q: in the literature there are cases of increased international normalised ratio in patients maintained on acenocoumarol or warfarin and prescribed a course of amoxicillin
If co-administration is necessary, the prothrombin time or international normalised ratio should be carefully monitored with the addition or withdrawal of amoxicillin.

items.t: Methotrexate: penicillins may reduce methotrexate excretion and increase toxicity. SPS: for short penicillin courses (up to 10 days) consider using with caution and monitor for toxicity (sore throat, bruising, bleeding).

src.q: Penicillins may reduce the excretion of methotrexate causing a potential increase in toxicity.
If the duration of penicillin is short (up to 10 days), consider using with caution and advise to monitor for signs of toxicity.

items.t: Probenecid: concomitant use not recommended (raises and prolongs amoxicillin levels).

src.q: Probenecid Concomitant use of probenecid is not recommended.

items.t: Allopurinol: increased likelihood of allergic skin reactions.

src.q: Concurrent administration of allopurinol during treatment with amoxicillin can increase the likelihood of allergic skin reactions.

items.t: Tetracyclines and other bacteriostatic drugs may interfere with amoxicillin's bactericidal effect.

src.q: Tetracyclines and other bacteriostatic drugs may interfere with the bactericidal effects of amoxicillin.

items.t: Oral typhoid vaccine is inactivated by antibacterials.

src.q: The oral typhoid vaccine is inactivated by antibacterials.

items.t: GFR > 30 ml/min: no adjustment.

src.q: greater than 30 No adjustment necessary No adjustment necessary

items.t: GFR 10 to 30 ml/min: adults and children ≥ 40 kg maximum 500 mg twice daily; children < 40 kg 15 mg/kg twice daily (maximum 500 mg twice daily).

src.q: 10 to 30 Maximum 500 mg twice daily 15 mg/kg given twice daily (maximum 500 mg twice daily)

items.t: GFR < 10 ml/min: adults and children ≥ 40 kg maximum 500 mg/day; children < 40 kg 15 mg/kg as a single dose (maximum 500 mg). For children < 40 kg parenteral therapy is preferred in most cases.

src.q: less than 10 Maximum 500 mg/day 15 mg/kg given as a single dose (maximum 500 mg)
In the majority of cases, parenteral therapy is preferred.

items.t: Haemodialysis: adults/children > 40 kg 500 mg every 24 h, plus one extra 500 mg dose before and another 500 mg dose after dialysis. Children < 40 kg 15 mg/kg/day once daily (maximum 500 mg), plus 15 mg/kg before and after dialysis. Peritoneal dialysis: maximum 500 mg/day.

src.q: Haemodialysis Adults and children over 40 kg 500 mg every 24 h Prior to haemodialysis one additional dose of 500 mg should be administered.
Children under 40 kg 15 mg/kg/day given as a single daily dose (maximum 500 mg).
In patients receiving peritoneal dialysis Amoxicillin maximum 500 mg/day.

items.t: Hepatic impairment: dose with caution and monitor hepatic function at regular intervals.

src.q: Hepatic impairment Dose with caution and monitor hepatic function at regular intervals

items.t: SmPC: limited human data do not indicate an increased risk of congenital malformations; may be used when potential benefits outweigh potential risks.

src.q: Limited data on the use of amoxicillin during pregnancy in humans do not indicate an increased risk of congenital malformations.
Amoxicillin may be used in pregnancy when the potential benefits outweigh the potential risks associated with treatment.

items.t: BUMPS (UKTIS): amoxicillin can be taken in pregnancy if recommended by a doctor; no concerns that penicillin use will harm the baby; no extra monitoring for major birth defects needed.

src.q: Amoxicillin, co-amoxiclav, and penicillin V can be taken in pregnancy if recommended by a doctor.
There are no concerns that use of a penicillin antibiotic in pregnancy will harm your baby.

items.t: SmPC: excreted in breast milk in small amounts (possible sensitisation, diarrhoea and mucosal fungal infection in the infant); use only after benefit/risk assessment.

src.q: Amoxicillin is excreted into breast milk in small quantities with the possible risk of sensitisation.
Amoxicillin should only be used during breast-feeding after benefit/risk assessment by the physician in charge.

items.t: SPS: all penicillins can be used during breastfeeding with precautionary infant monitoring; amoxicillin is a preferred choice. Monitor the infant for GI disturbance, oral candida, hypersensitivity (rash, breathing problems), nausea, irritability and drowsiness.

src.q: All penicillin antibiotics can be used during breastfeeding with precautionary infant monitoring.
the broad-spectrum penicillins, such as amoxicillin and ampicillin, are the preferred choices
As a precaution, monitor for gastro-intestinal disturbances, oral candida infection, hypersensitivity reactions (including rashes or breathing problems), nausea, irritability, and drowsiness.

items.t: No human fertility data; animal reproductive studies showed no effect on fertility.

src.q: There are no data on the effects of amoxicillin on fertility in humans. Reproductive studies in animals have shown no effects on fertility.

items.t: Common: diarrhoea, nausea, skin rash. Uncommon: vomiting, urticaria, pruritus.

src.q: The most commonly reported adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are diarrhoea, nausea and skin rash.
*Common Diarrhoea and nausea *Uncommon Vomiting
*Common Skin rash *Uncommon Urticaria and pruritus

items.t: Severe allergic reactions (angioedema, anaphylaxis, serum sickness, hypersensitivity vasculitis): stop amoxicillin and start appropriate alternative therapy.

src.q: Severe allergic reactions, including angioneurotic oedema, anaphylaxis, serum sickness and hypersensitivity vasculitis
If an allergic reaction occurs, amoxicillin therapy must be discontinued and appropriate alternative therapy instituted.

items.t: Severe skin reactions (erythema multiforme, SJS, TEN, bullous/exfoliative dermatitis, AGEP, DRESS). AGEP requires stopping and contraindicates future use.

src.q: Skin reactions such as erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, bullous and exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP)
This reaction requires amoxicillin discontinuation and contra-indicates any subsequent administration.

items.t: Antibiotic-associated colitis (including pseudomembranous colitis): stop immediately and seek medical review.

src.q: Should antibiotic-associated colitis occur, amoxicillin should immediately be discontinued, a physician consulted and an appropriate therapy initiated.

Reversible leucopenia (including severe neutropenia or agranulocytosis), reversible thrombocytopenia and haemolytic anaemia.
Very rare Interstitial nephritis Not known Crystalluria (including acute renal injury)

items.t: Prolonged therapy: periodic assessment of renal, hepatic and haematopoietic function is advisable.

src.q: Periodic assessment of organ system functions; including renal, hepatic and haematopoietic function is advisable during prolonged therapy.

src.q: Appropriate monitoring should be undertaken when anticoagulants are prescribed concomitantly.

src.q: Hepatically impaired patients should be dosed with caution and hepatic function monitored at regular intervals.

This reaction requires amoxicillin discontinuation
